changelog: Core Principles: Emphasised that ranking should demote candidates where remaining words can change agent, polarity, head noun, pronoun antecedent, modifier attachment, or verb sense — to focus fixes on placement errors rather than candidacy.

When to Segment: Made candidacy rules more explicit about safe surface signals and added a short, explicit list of common disambiguating follow-ups (relative/complementizers, negation, postverbal obliques, short temporal/prepositional fragments, range markers, vague pronouns) that should be treated as likely to overturn prior text and therefore ranked lower.

Priority Rules: Tightened the positive criterion for top-ranked cuts: prefer cuts only when the preceding stretch contains a stable predication with its core participants or a self-contained adjunct; added concrete demotion signals (e.g., a comma followed by a relative pronoun, or an immediate following token from the disambiguating list) so risky boundaries are ranked lower rather than removed.

Decision Procedure: Clarified the two-step flow: mark generously, then place risky candidates low; explicitly instruct demotion (not forbidding) for boundaries that end immediately before the listed disambiguating signals and to supply conservative, low-confidence candidates at safe punctuation/conjunctions only when needed to meet the minimum-tag requirement.
